subject.title: perf(anthropic): memoize the local Claude session scan

question: Should OpenClaw accept a five-second cached Claude session catalog as the default freshness contract for local session selection?
rationale: The implementation deliberately trades immediate catalog freshness for polling performance; this is a user-visible session-discovery policy choice that tests alone cannot calibrate across real Claude directory behavior.

options.title: Accept bounded staleness with live proof
options.body: Accept the five-second cache after reviewing redacted real-run evidence that repeat polls avoid the expensive scan and a newly created session remains openable.

options.title: Require stricter freshness
options.body: Request a narrower cache or an explicit invalidation mechanism if five seconds is not acceptable for the session-selection experience.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded staleness with live proof
recommendation.body: Accept the five-second cache after reviewing redacted real-run evidence that repeat polls avoid the expensive scan and a newly created session remains openable.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the only directly evidenced contributor for the affected session-catalog change.
